A) Invariants (treated as hard constraints)

Evening: non-work, low activation. Caffeine cutoff per P1.
~60–90 minutes pre-bed: Rumination protocol (below).
Lights-out: fixed.

D) Rumination protocol (designed as a control loop, not a debate)
Goal: reduce time spent in unbounded checking/mental simulation.
1) “Worry capture” (3 minutes): write the loop in one sentence, plus the smallest falsifiable check (e.g., “Confirm the randomization procedure is described with seed handling.”).
2) “Time-boxed check planning” (4 minutes): schedule that check into a specific slot tomorrow (ideally inside Deep Work Block 2), and define the stopping rule (what evidence counts as ‘done’).
3) “Cognitive off-ramp” (5 minutes): low-stimulation activity (paper book, breathing cadence, shower). No screens.
If you wake and the loop restarts: repeat capture on paper; no method-section edits at 02:00 (this is an invariant).

E) Daily progress artifact (to satisfy PI with minimal cognitive tax)
Send one email/Slack message, same time each day, with a fixed schema:
- “Today completed:” 3 bullets (observable outputs: pages revised, figure updated, analysis run).
- “Blocked by:” 0–2 bullets (with next action).
- “Tomorrow plan:” 3 bullets.
This converts “daily proof of work” into a low-variance routine.

F) Lightweight verification / tracking (so you can actually test whether it works)
One sheet per day, 2 minutes at lunch + 3 minutes at shutdown:
Metrics (binary or small integers; avoid elaborate journaling):
1) Deep work blocks achieved: 0/1/2.
2) Total comms minutes (estimate): <30, 30–45, 45–60, >60.
3) Sleep: lights-out time, wake time, and rumination minutes (estimate).
4) Mode switches count (analysis/writing/admin): integer.
5) Output tokens: e.g., “words edited” (rough) + “figures advanced” (0/1).
Then a weekly review every 3–4 days during this sprint: look for which invariant is failing first (sleep drift? comms leakage? meetings splintering?). Adjust only one parameter at a time (P1–P5) so you can attribute causality.
